subject: serval
title: This Cat Catches Its Meal Every Second Try. Lions Manage About 1 in 4

scenes.text: This cat wins about half its hunts. A lion gets roughly one in four.
The serval has the longest legs of any cat for its body size.
Each huge ear has twenty-two muscles and can swivel to hear a rodent moving underground.
Then it leaps. From a standstill, it can jump about three meters straight up and snatch birds out of the air.
It can pounce on prey from up to four meters away.
In one Tanzanian crater, servals caught about half of everything they chased, and most rodents they went for. Lions, about a quarter.

description:
Servals succeed in about half of their hunts (around 50% in Ngorongoro Crater, up to 81% for rodents alone), compared with roughly 20-30% for lions.
They have the longest legs of any cat relative to body size, ears with 22 muscles that locate prey underground, and can leap about 3 m straight up from a standstill to catch birds.
Which cat would you bet on in a hunting contest?
first_comment: Rodents make up 80 to 90 percent of a serval's diet. What's the best hunter in the animal kingdom, in your opinion?
